action.title: Root analysis

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc Pro B70/XPU Triton likely favors dense block matmul-style work and fp16 dot paths; fixed C=32, N=16, hidden=128 are small enough for specialization but may stress register files if fully fused.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The workload mixes reductions, small-window attention, dense per-token linear layers, layernorm, residuals, and GELU. Dense MLP/projection math dominates total FLOPs, while many small eager kernels and layout reshapes likely dominate latency in PyTorch.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Triton XPU codegen quality for small fixed reductions and fp16 dot accumulation may differ significantly from CUDA expectations.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input/output tensor is NHWC contiguous with 921600 tokens and C=32, about 59 MB per full fp16 tensor. Naive eager materializes norm1, qkv, attention output, proj, residual, norm2, fc1, activation, fc2, causing large intermediate traffic. Fusion can reduce bandwidth substantially.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Full fusion may reduce traffic but lose optimized GEMM reuse; partial fusion may leave most memory traffic intact.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window full fusion wants to hold 16x32 normalized values, q/k/v, attention logits/probabilities, projection partials, and MLP partials; this is attractive because sizes are fixed but can exceed practical register budgets.
register_pressure.risk: A single monolithic Triton program may spill or reduce occupancy, especially around qkv, attention, and hidden=128 MLP accumulation.

nodes.notes: Latest evidence: the active full-window-owned Triton prototype failed evaluation with SIGSEGV. The search should pivot away from highly fused XPU Triton kernels and prioritize simpler staged designs with lower register pressure and better backend robustness.

action.description: Implement a specialized fused Triton path that owns one or more complete 4x4 windows and performs norm1, qkv, attention, projection, residual, norm2, fc1, GELU, fc2, and final residual directly from/to NHWC.
action.rationale: The fixed small dimensions allow aggressive specialization and avoid most eager intermediate tensors and launch overhead. If register usage is acceptable, this is the highest-upside path.
action.title: Full block window-owned fused implementation

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Maps naturally to independent windows; fixed 16-token attention and C=32 reductions fit specialization. Dense MLP hidden=128 may or may not map efficiently to XPU dot hardware from a single-window program.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The B70 may not benefit if fusion prevents dense phases from using optimized matrix paths; correctness risk is also high after the simpler staged failure.

memory_bandwidth.notes: A successful full fused window-owned design could reduce intermediate writes substantially, but only after exact reference semantics are solved.

register_pressure.notes: Owning attention, projection, LayerNorm, GELU, MLP, and residuals in larger fused regions is likely to exceed comfortable register/shared-memory budgets.

action.description: Implement a staged ModelNew that keeps the large dense linear/MLP phases as efficient batched operations while adding Triton kernels for fused layernorm/residual/GELU and a compact custom window-attention phase.
action.rationale: This lowers implementation risk and preserves high-throughput dense matrix multiplication for qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 while reducing Python/kernel overhead around normalization, residuals, and attention layout.
action.title: Prototype GEMM-centered staged block

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Likely fits Intel XPU backend better for large token-batched dense layers: matrices are roughly 921600x32 by 32x96, 921600x32 by 32x128, and 921600x128 by 128x32.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Dense projections can fit Arc matrix hardware through torch backends, but the submitted path did not implement the intended fused LN/GELU/attention kernels and failed correctness before performance could be measured.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The attempted implementation leaves most large tensor traffic in PyTorch eager ops and only optionally fuses add, so bandwidth savings are minimal.

register_pressure.notes: Register pressure is not the immediate failure mode because the custom Triton portion is only a simple add kernel; a real fused staged path would increase pressure.

action.description: Implement only the custom 4x4 single-head window-attention Triton kernel, including direct NHWC/window indexing, rpe add, stable softmax over 16, and attention-value product, while leaving layernorm and MLP/projection paths close to the reference.
action.rationale: This is the smallest correctness-risk custom kernel and directly targets the unusual Swin-specific part where generic PyTorch may spend overhead on reshape/permute/softmax for tiny windows.
action.title: Prototype attention-centered custom path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Small 16x16 attention per window is naturally independent but not very compute-heavy; XPU occupancy depends on batching many windows efficiently.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The attention work per window is small, but owning it directly may avoid launch/layout overhead while leaving dense GEMMs to optimized libraries.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Customizing only the small 4x4 window attention can reduce reshape/attention overhead without disturbing the large MLP and projection code paths.

register_pressure.notes: A 16-token, C=32 single-head attention kernel is compact enough to keep register pressure moderate on Arc, provided softmax is handled carefully.

action.rationale: The MLP is likely the largest FLOP and memory component. Specializing C=32 and hidden=128 may reduce intermediate fc1/GELU traffic and improve latency even if attention remains separate.
action.title: Prototype MLP-centered custom path

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Per-token dense reductions 32->128->32 have enough repeated tokens to amortize weight loads, but a hand Triton kernel must compete with efficient GEMM paths on XPU.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Targets the numerically regular, dense, high-FLOP portion of the model and avoids storing the large hidden activation if fully streamed.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Custom token-wise MLP may underutilize dot hardware compared with large GEMM, especially for fc1/fc2.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Potentially removes the very large fc1 activation and GELU intermediate, which are about 236 MB each in fp16 for [921600,128].
memory_bandwidth.risk: If hidden dimension is tiled and partial fc2 accumulation requires multiple passes, extra reads/writes may reduce savings.

register_pressure.risk: Holding too many hidden channels per token can spill; tiling hidden channels complicates fc2 accumulation.

kernel_summary: The workload is a fixed-shape fp16 NHWC simplified Swin block over 921600 tokens with 57600 independent 4x4 windows, C=32, one head, and hidden=128. It combines two fp32-accumulated layernorm reductions, small N=16 attention with softmax and rpe, four dense linear layers, GELU, and residuals. The main optimization opportunity is eliminating eager intermediate tensors and launch/layout overhead while preserving enough dense-math efficiency on Intel XPU; the main risks are register pressure in a fully fused per-window kernel, numerical mismatch for LayerNorm/GELU/softmax, and underperforming optimized GEMM paths for the large MLP/projection phases.
open_questions: What correctness tolerance will be used, especially for fp16 output when LayerNorm, softmax, linear accumulation, and GELU may differ from PyTorch/XPU numerics?
Does Triton on Intel Arc Pro B70 provide efficient fp16 tl.dot lowering for the small fixed shapes C=32, N=16, and hidden=128, or will custom dense reductions scalarize poorly?
Are ModelNew implementations allowed to call torch.nn.functional.linear or module Linear for some phases, or must all performance-critical phases be Triton-only?
What is the actual reference and torch.compile latency on the target XPU, and which phase dominates in profiling: layernorm, qkv/proj, attention, MLP, or memory layout operations?
What are the practical register and shared/local memory limits per Triton program on this XPU backend for a monolithic 16-token fused window kernel?
Is rpe_bias loaded as fp16 after self.half() in evaluation, and must its addition match PyTorch promotion/casting exactly?
Does PyTorch GELU use exact erf behavior in the evaluator, and is a tanh approximation acceptable within tolerance?
Are H, W, B, C, window size, and mlp_ratio always exactly the provided values, or must the submitted class handle other compatible runtime shapes?
